name: morphing-weather
title: Morphing weather: one icon path that morphs between sun, cloud, rain, snow and storm
summary: A weather screen whose big icon is a single path morphing pairwise between five outlines (sun disc, cloud, rain cloud, snow cloud, storm anvil) with an eased blend, whether the host changes the condition or a day is tapped in the forecast strip. Spinning sun rays, falling rain, drifting snow and a flickering bolt fade in with their condition, the sky gradient and the icon's colours blend along, and the temperature, high/low, wind, humidity and rain chance count to the new day's values. One canvas lays out a phone screen or, when wide or short, a 4x2 widget.
prompt: A weather screen whose big icon morphs smoothly between sun, cloud, rain, snow and storm when the condition changes or when I tap a day in the forecast strip, with animated details (spinning sun rays, falling drops), the temperature counting to the new value and the background gradient shifting. It should also work as a 4x2 widget.
hand_built: The morph is the point: five same-shaped outlines blended by eased per-condition weights through a chain of pathTweens, which no library component does (WeatherIcon switches icons; it does not morph)
teaches: Pairwise morph between any two of five paths: give each condition an eased weight w_i = anim(1 - min(1, |c - i|)); when c jumps from a to b, w_a eases 1 to 0 while w_b eases 0 to 1 on the same curve, so the blend is a pure a to b morph even from sun straight to storm

Turn the five weights into a chain of four pathTweens: m1 = tween(s0, s1, k1), m2 = tween(m1, s2, k2), ... with k_i = w_i / (w_0 + ... + w_i); the last tween gives every outline exactly its weight. A pathTween output can feed the next pathTween in both players

Make outlines that morph well by sampling each shape the same way: here every outline is 28 cubic segments through points ray-cast from one centre at the same 28 angles, so point k of the sun sits at the same angle as point k of every cloud

Blend colours without colour expressions: draw the morphing path (and the sky rectangle) once per condition, each with its own gradient and paint alpha k_i, the same chain values: layer i over the previous ones leaves exactly weight w_i of its colour

Details that belong to one condition (rays, drops, flakes, bolt) are drawn always with alpha w_i, so they fade with the morph; loops over 7 to 12 items with fract(t * speed + i * 0.382) phases make the rain and snow
The temperature, high/low and stats are anim'd values ({value, anim: 0.9}) printed with textFromFloat: the number counts to the new value

One canvas does both layouts: wide = max(step(W / heroHeight, 1.6), step(400, heroHeight)) picks the widget arrangement (icon left, text right) over the phone one, and the two text blocks are scaled by wide and 1 - wide
The forecast strip is drawn in the canvas; its tap targets are five transparent weighted boxes over it in a column, each with semantics and valueFloatChange sel = i
pitfalls: The outlines must have the same verbs and point count: all five are moveTo + 28 cubicTo + close. A shape that is not star-shaped from the ray-cast centre (an overhang) loses its concave part

pathTween tweens linearly; the easing comes from the weights, which are anim'd values (the default anim easing). An anim on the condition index itself would morph through the intermediate shapes (sun to storm via cloud, rain and snow)
Paint alpha is reset by a following color op in the same paint: set alpha in every paint that sets a colour
Expressions are capped at 32 entries on Android: the chain weights are split into ws, k1..k4
The clickable boxes get the player's press feedback (a light disc at the tap point for a few frames, in both players), drawn over the canvas
The TS harness in players/typescript/render.mjs pins the clock without advancing it; to see the morph frames in TS use the inspector (interact) or advance the clock per frame

snippets.note: w0: an eased weight per condition
the first pathTween of the chain sun -> cloud by k1
the last pathTween: body, drawn five times with chain alphas
the temperature counts to the selected day's value
the host sets the current condition (0..4); arrays fc/hi/lo/wind/hum/rain carry the forecast

condition.meaning: the current condition: 0 sun, 1 cloud, 2 rain, 3 snow, 4 storm

sel.meaning: the selected day, 0 (now) to 4; taps set it

fc.meaning: condition of the next four days (0..4)

hi.meaning: high temperature, today and the next four days

inputs.clock: the date line and the weekday names of the strip

check.describe: Clock pinned to Monday 2 November 2026. 360x640: Lyon, Monday · 2 November, a sun with 12 rays on a blue sky, 12°, Sunny, H 14° L 4°, wind/humidity/rain, and a strip Now Tue Wed Thu Fri with mini icons and highs. condition 2/3/4: the same screen with a rain cloud and falling drops on a dark slate sky, a snow cloud with flakes, a dark anvil with a yellow bolt on a near-black sky. morph: 0.3 s after tapping Wed the disc is half-way to the rain cloud, rays shrinking, drops appearing, sky darkening, the number counting down. tapped-storm: Thursday selected, storm icon, 10°. Widgets 360x180 and 400x200: icon left, big temperature and condition, city/day/high-low right, the strip below. 300x300 uses the widget arrangement; 412x915 the phone one.
